reviewer: Kimi independent actual visual comparison of the exact 65x67 source PNG, enlarged existing source-page 06, complete unchanged 2048x2048 raw RGBA, full white/cyan/alpha review sheet and unchanged naiwa.png mascot reference; checked cap, covered hair, brows, absence of added facial hair, one mouth, eyewear, uniform/collar/ribbon/pendant counts, pose, crop, lighting, collar fit, complete card/note/backplate and visible transparency.

entries.positive_observation: The field-gray/olive peaked cap with small gold front insignia and gold visor leaves, covered hair and light-brown eyebrows remain. The face has a smooth chin and no added moustache or beard, one serious closed mouth and no spectacles. The nearly frontal capped head turned subtly toward viewer left, matching gaze, squared shoulders, chest-up crop and directional facial light with visor shadow are preserved. The olive uniform keeps two red collar patches with gold details, one gold-edged shoulder board at viewer left, one pale blue-white neck ribbon and one silver-toned cross-shaped pendant; no extra medal or eyewear was added. The high collar and throat decoration fit coherently around a short broad neck beneath the rounded chin, without a long yellow column, pinching, clipping or cream bib. The complete tilted dark frame, opaque muted gray-olive photographic backplate, overlapping warm-cream note with faint upper marks and mostly blank lower paper, and small dark right-edge tab remain. Full white/cyan inspection shows a genuine transparent exterior with no visible interior holes, missing backing or working-matte halo.
entries.alpha_decision: Accept native RGBA extrema 0..254 after actual white/cyan/alpha viewing rather than numeric screening alone; no source-alpha replacement was performed or needed.
entries.visible_limitations: At 65x67 very fine upper-lip hair and exact cap, collar and pendant insignia are not reliably readable; the review found no clear added facial hair and compared only visible colors, forms and placements without inventing more specific emblems. Note marks remain indistinct visual groups rather than readable text.
